edits.text:
# Forkify V2 Deployment Repository Separation Strategy

## Objective

Keep the application codebase and infrastructure codebase decoupled so each repository has a single responsibility and can evolve independently.

## Repository split

### Application repository
This repository will remain responsible for:
- frontend source code
- backend source code
- database schema and migration assets
- local Docker Compose for development
- CI definitions for automated validation
- release documentation and architecture notes

### Deployment repository
A separate repository will be responsible for:
- Kubernetes manifests
- Helm charts or Kustomize overlays
- Terraform modules and state management
- cloud provider configuration
- secrets and environment management
- production deployment automation

## Why this separation matters

- keeps application development independent from infrastructure provisioning
- reduces accidental coupling between runtime code and deployment configuration
- allows different release cadences for app changes and infrastructure changes
- makes it easier to reuse the app repository across multiple deployment targets

## Boundaries for this repo

This repository should stay focused on application delivery and local validation only. Infrastructure ownership should not be mixed into application code reviews or feature branches.

## Recommended future process

1. Feature work happens in the application repository.
2. Docker and CI validation run here.
3. Deployment artifacts are generated or referenced from the deployment repository.
4. Infra changes are reviewed and applied there, separately from app changes.

## Governance note

The application repository may include Docker compose and local environment files, but it should not contain the live cloud deployment state or Kubernetes production configuration.

{"filePath":"/workspaces/Forkity-V2/docs/session-notes/forkity-deployment-separation.md","content":"# Forkify V2 Deployment Repository Separation Strategy

## Objective

Keep the application codebase and infrastructure codebase decoupled so each repository has a single responsibility and can evolve independently.

## Repository split

### Application repository
This repository will remain responsible for:
- frontend source code
- backend source code
- database schema and migration assets
- local Docker Compose for development
- CI definitions for automated validation
- release documentation and architecture notes

### Deployment repository
A separate repository will be responsible for:
- Kubernetes manifests
- Helm charts or Kustomize overlays
- Terraform modules and state management
- cloud provider configuration
- secrets and environment management
- production deployment automation

## Why this separation matters

- keeps application development independent from infrastructure provisioning
- reduces accidental coupling between runtime code and deployment configuration
- allows different release cadences for app changes and infrastructure changes
- makes it easier to reuse the app repository across multiple deployment targets

## Boundaries for this repo

This repository should stay focused on application delivery and local validation only. Infrastructure ownership should not be mixed into application code reviews or feature branches.

## Recommended future process

1. Feature work happens in the application repository.
2. Docker and CI validation run here.
3. Deployment artifacts are generated or referenced from the deployment repository.
4. Infra changes are reviewed and applied there, separately from app changes.

## Governance note

The application repository may include Docker compose and local environment files, but it should not contain the live cloud deployment state or Kubernetes production configuration.
"}

{"filePath":"/workspaces/Forkity-V2/database/prisma/schema.prisma","content":"generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

model User {
  id           String    @id @default(cuid())
  email        String    @unique
  name         String?
  passwordHash String
  createdAt    DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt    DateTime  @updatedAt
  bookmarks    Bookmark[]
  recipes      Recipe[]
}

model Recipe {
  id          String    @id @default(cuid())
  title       String
  sourceUrl   String
  imageUrl    String?
  publisher   String
  cookingTime Int
  servings    Int
  ingredients Json
  createdAt   DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime  @updatedAt
  userId      String?
  user        User?     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)
  bookmarks   Bookmark[]
}

model Bookmark {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  userId    String
  recipeId  String
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  user      User     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  recipe    Recipe   @relation(fields: [recipeId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@unique([userId, recipeId])
}
"}

summaries.text:
1. Conversation Overview:
- Primary Objectives:
  - "Check all the README.md files in this directory and understand the context and the stage where we left off at the last time."
  - "So lets begin stage 3."
  - "From now on when we finish a stage please let me know what the next stage is and check that I understand it and ask for permission to move on to the next step."
  - "Before we continue, can you generate text for the commit to github?" and "please make it more technical"
  - "Lets continue to stage 5", "Lets continue with stage 6", "continue with step 7", "Please proceed with step 8"
  - "Yes, please continue." / "Please continue" as the final active direction
- Session Context:
  - This started with repo discovery and project-state reconstruction. It later evolved into a staged implementation plan: Stage 3 functional frontend work, Stage 4 validation, Stage 5 Dockerization, Stage 6 Jenkins CI, Stage 7 deployment separation, Stage 8 backend/database, and then integration polish.
- User Intent Evolution:
  - Started with context gathering and sequencing
  - Moved into implementation by stage
  - Added workflow discipline for stage transitions
  - Concluded with live integration and final polish objectives

2. Technical Foundation:
- Frontend:
  - Vanilla JavaScript app with Parcel, ES modules, HTML/CSS shell
  - MVC structure centered around [frontend/js/model.js](frontend/js/model.js), [frontend/js/controller.js](frontend/js/controller.js), and [frontend/js/views](frontend/js/views)
- Backend:
  - Express server in [backend/src/server.js](backend/src/server.js)
  - Prisma + PostgreSQL database via [database/prisma/schema.prisma](database/prisma/schema.prisma)
- Database:
  - PostgreSQL 16 via Docker Compose service in [docker-compose.yml](docker-compose.yml)
  - Initial migration in [database/prisma/migrations/20260924_init/migration.sql](database/prisma/migrations/20260924_init/migration.sql)
- CI:
  - Jenkins declarative pipeline in [Jenkinsfile](Jenkinsfile)
- Architecture:
  - App logic separated from infrastructure; deployment repo split documented in [docs/session-notes/forkity-deployment-separation.md](docs/session-notes/forkity-deployment-separation.md)
- Environment:
  - Frontend runs on port 1234
  - Backend runs on port 4000
  - Database runs on port 5432
  - External recipe API proxied through backend to maintain app API conventions

3. Codebase Status:
- [README.md](README.md):
  - Purpose: strategic roadmap and project boundaries
  - Current State: still documents long-range architecture, but session notes capture actual progress
- [backend/README.md](backend/README.md):
  - Purpose: backend responsibilities and setup
  - Current State: updated to reflect real implementation and API endpoints
- [database/README.md](database/README.md):
  - Purpose: Prisma/Postgres foundation documentation
  - Current State: updated to reflect migration and local DB usage
- [docs/session-notes/forkity-plan.md](docs/session-notes/forkity-plan.md):
  - Purpose: planned roadmap and stage sequence
  - Current State: updated to reflect actual progress up to Stage 8
- [docs/session-notes/forkity-progress.md](docs/session-notes/forkity-progress.md):
  - Purpose: live project status and verification notes
  - Current State: documents completed stages and remaining integration polish
- [frontend/js/model.js](frontend/js/model.js):
  - Purpose: core app state, recipe loading, bookmark persistence, user session, servings updates
  - Current State: stable and integration-ready; supports persisted user/bookmark flow
  - Key Code Segments:
    - createRecipeObject
    - loadRecipe
    - loadSearchResults
    - updateServings
    - addBookmark
    - deleteBookmark
    - initializeUser
    - syncBookmarks
- [frontend/js/controller.js](frontend/js/controller.js):
  - Purpose: orchestrates model/view interaction
  - Current State: async bookmark flow integrated
- [backend/src/server.js](backend/src/server.js):
  - Purpose: Express endpoints for health, users, recipes, bookmarks, and proxying external search/detail requests
  - Current State: validated and serving live data
- [database/prisma/schema.prisma](database/prisma/schema.prisma):
  - Purpose: Prisma schema for User, Recipe, Bookmark
  - Current State: database synced and valid
- [Jenkinsfile](Jenkinsfile):
  - Purpose: CI pipeline for dependency install, tests, build, artifact archiving
  - Current State: complete and validated
- [docker-compose.yml](docker-compose.yml):
  - Purpose: local database and frontend container orchestration
  - Current State: working; DB service active
- [frontend/Dockerfile](frontend/Dockerfile):
  - Purpose: frontend container image
  - Current State: built successfully
- [frontend/tests/bookmarks.test.mjs](frontend/tests/bookmarks.test.mjs):
  - Purpose: regression coverage for bookmark and servings logic
  - Current State: passing
- [frontend/tests/userFlow.test.mjs](frontend/tests/userFlow.test.mjs):
  - Purpose: regression coverage for persisted user/session flow
  - Current State: passing

4. Problem Resolution:
- Issues Encountered:
  - README files still described future architecture while actual work was already in progress.
  - Duplicate bookmarks and invalid delete handling.
  - Search input blank/whitespace issues.
  - Stale port 4000 conflicts when restarting backend.
  - Async test mismatch with new async bookmark logic.
  - Prisma validation failed without DATABASE_URL.
  - External Forkify API key was required for recipe search/detail proxying.
- Solutions Implemented:
  - Session notes were used to distinguish roadmap from actual status.
  - Bookmark logic was hardened to prevent duplicates and ignore invalid deletes.
  - Search input was trimmed before processing.
  - Docker and Jenkins were added once the app reached a stable local state.
  - Database env files and runtime configuration were fixed.
  - API key was added to backend environment and verified live.
  - Tests were rewritten to reflect async flow and mocked API behavior when appropriate.
- Debugging Context:
  - Reproduced failures via targeted tests before fixing them.
  - Used live curl checks against backend health and recipe search endpoints.
  - Cleared stale Node processes bound to port 4000.
- Lessons Learned:
  - Staged progression kept the project coherent.
  - Backend and DB work were necessary before final integration polish.
  - Local validation must precede CI and deployment separation.

5. Progress Tracking:
- Completed Tasks:
  - README review and context restoration
  - Stage 3 bookmark logic stabilization
  - Stage 4 search flow validation
  - Stage 5 Docker local environment
  - Stage 6 Jenkins CI
  - Stage 7 deployment separation strategy
  - Stage 8 backend and database foundation
  - Live frontend-backend integration
  - User/session persistence
  - Full validation with tests and build
- Partially Complete Work:
  - final local orchestration/run scripts to simplify multi-process startup
  - end-to-end polish for a single-command full-stack developer experience
- Validated Outcomes:
  - Frontend test command passes: 4 passing tests, 0 failing
  - Frontend build succeeds
  - Prisma schema validates and database syncs successfully
  - Backend health endpoint returns connected status
  - User creation via API succeeds
  - Recipe search endpoint returns live data

6. Active Work State:
- Current Focus:
  - Final end-to-end polish and local orchestration of full-stack app startup
- Recent Context:
  - User repeatedly confirmed progression and requested continuation after each stage
  - Most recent work was focused on live stack validation and making the workflow easier to run in a single terminal
- Working Code:
  - Current codebase already includes working backend, database, frontend, Docker, Jenkins, and integration state
  - The remaining polish is a root-level orchestration script and final local workflow cleanup

# Forkify V2

Forkify V2 is a full-stack redesign of the recipe application originally built during Jonas Schmedtmann's JavaScript course.

## Project boundaries

- `frontend/`: current browser application and Parcel development server
- `backend/`: Express API for users, recipes, and bookmarks
- `database/`: PostgreSQL and Prisma schema/migration assets
- `docs/`: architecture documentation and diagrams

## Local development

Start the full local stack with:

```bash
npm run db
npm run dev
```

The frontend is available at `http://localhost:1234` and the backend at `http://localhost:4000`.

## Development sequence

1. Establish the application architecture and preserve the approved visual direction.
2. Migrate the frontend design into React components.
3. Implement the backend API and authentication. (Complete)
4. Add PostgreSQL persistence through Prisma. (Complete)
5. Connect frontend workflows to the backend. (Complete)
6. Add Docker for local and reproducible environments. (Complete)
7. Add Jenkins CI only after the application and design are fully functional. (Complete)

Cloud infrastructure, Terraform, and Kubernetes will be maintained later in a separate deployment repository.

edits.text:
# Forkify V2

Forkify V2 is a full-stack redesign of the recipe application originally built during Jonas Schmedtmann's JavaScript course.

## Project boundaries

- `frontend/`: current browser application and Parcel development server
- `backend/`: Express API for users, recipes, and bookmarks
- `database/`: PostgreSQL and Prisma schema/migration assets
- `docs/`: architecture documentation and diagrams

## Local development

Start the full local stack with:

```bash
npm start
```

The frontend is available at `http://localhost:1234` and the backend at `http://localhost:4000`.

## Development sequence

1. Establish the application architecture and preserve the approved visual direction.
2. Migrate the frontend design into React components.
3. Implement the backend API and authentication. (Complete)
4. Add PostgreSQL persistence through Prisma. (Complete)
5. Connect frontend workflows to the backend. (Complete)
6. Add Docker for local and reproducible environments. (Complete)
7. Add Jenkins CI only after the application and design are fully functional. (Complete)

Cloud infrastructure, Terraform, and Kubernetes will be maintained later in a separate deployment repository.

# Forkify V2 Current Progress

## Date
- 2026-09-23

## Status
- Stages 2 through 8 are complete.
- Frontend, backend, PostgreSQL, Docker, Jenkins, and deployment separation are integrated.
- Final local orchestration is available through the root `npm start` command.
- Design polishing remains intentionally deferred until a later stage.

## Completed work
- Reviewed app scope and architecture.
- Confirmed user management and bookmarks are required in the future data model.
- Saved the project plan in the session notes.
- Built the landing-page app shell in frontend/index.html.
- Fixed the view clear/render issue in frontend/js/views/view.js.
- Added upload guard safety in frontend/js/utils/uploadGuard.js.
- Updated add-recipe modal logic in frontend/js/views/addRecipeView.js.
- Added smoke test coverage in frontend/tests/uploadGuard.test.mjs.
- Verified with: npm test and npm run build.

## Verification evidence
- Frontend tests: 4 passing tests, 0 failing tests
- Frontend build: Parcel build succeeded
- Prisma schema validation and database sync succeeded
- Backend health check returned `{"status":"ok","database":"connected"}`
- Root development workflow started backend on port 4000 and frontend on port 1234

## Next session target
- Continue with end-to-end feature polish and deployment preparation.

## Future phases planned
- backend and database integration with users and bookmarks
- deployment repo for Kubernetes + Terraform

services:
  frontend:
    build:
      context: ./frontend
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    container_name: forkity-frontend
    working_dir: /app
    ports:
      - "1234:1234"
    volumes:
      - ./frontend:/app
      - /app/node_modules
    command: npm run start -- --host 0.0.0.0

  backend:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: backend/Dockerfile
    container_name: forkity-backend
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://postgres:postgres@db:5432/forkity?schema=public
      PORT: 4000
      FORKIFY_API_KEY: ${FORKIFY_API_KEY:-}
    ports:
      - "4000:4000"
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      test:
        - CMD
        - node
        - -e
        - fetch('http://127.0.0.1:4000/api/health').then(r => process.exit(r.ok ? 0 : 1)).catch(() => process.exit(1))
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  db:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    container_name: forkity-db
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: forkity
      POSTGRES_USER: postgres
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U postgres -d forkity"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

volumes:
  postgres_data:

FROM node:20-alpine

WORKDIR /app

COPY backend/package*.json ./backend/
COPY database ./database

WORKDIR /app/backend
RUN npm install && npm run prisma:generate

COPY backend .

EXPOSE 4000

CMD ["npm", "start"]

# Backend

This directory contains the JavaScript API for users, recipes, and bookmarks.

Current responsibilities:

- Authentication and user management
- Recipe and bookmark endpoints
- Request validation and business rules
- Database access through Prisma and PostgreSQL
- Environment-based configuration

## Local setup

1. Copy the environment template:
   - `cp .env.example .env`
2. Ensure PostgreSQL is running locally or through Docker Compose.
3. Install dependencies:
   - `npm install`
4. Generate Prisma client:
   - `npm run prisma:generate`
5. Start the server:
   - `npm run dev`

The complete Docker Compose stack also includes the backend API and database:

```bash
docker compose up --build
```

The backend container waits for PostgreSQL readiness before starting and exposes port `4000`.

## API health check

- `GET /api/health`

## Core endpoints

- `GET /api/users`
- `POST /api/users`
- `GET /api/recipes`
- `POST /api/recipes`
- `GET /api/users/:userId/bookmarks`
- `POST /api/users/:userId/bookmarks/:recipeId`
- `DELETE /api/users/:userId/bookmarks/:recipeId`

WORKDIR /app

EXPOSE 4000

CMD ["npm", "start"]

# Forkify V2 Current Progress

## Date
- 2026-09-23

## Status
- Stages 2 through 8 are complete.
- Stage 9 is in progress: end-to-end polish and deployment preparation.
- Frontend, backend, PostgreSQL, Docker, Jenkins, and deployment separation are integrated.
- Final local orchestration is available through the root `npm start` command.
- Design polishing remains intentionally deferred until a later stage.

## Completed work
- Reviewed app scope and architecture.
- Confirmed user management and bookmarks are required in the future data model.
- Saved the project plan in the session notes.
- Built the landing-page app shell in frontend/index.html.
- Fixed the view clear/render issue in frontend/js/views/view.js.
- Added upload guard safety in frontend/js/utils/uploadGuard.js.
- Updated add-recipe modal logic in frontend/js/views/addRecipeView.js.
- Added smoke test coverage in frontend/tests/uploadGuard.test.mjs.
- Verified with: npm test and npm run build.

## Verification evidence
- Frontend tests: 4 passing tests, 0 failing tests
- Frontend build: Parcel build succeeded
- Prisma schema validation and database sync succeeded
- Backend health check returned `{"status":"ok","database":"connected"}`
- Root development workflow started backend on port 4000 and frontend on port 1234
- Backend Docker image builds successfully with Prisma and OpenSSL runtime support
- Compose configuration validates successfully
- Jenkins now validates frontend tests/build, backend syntax/Prisma schema, and Compose configuration

## Current stage note
- The backend container health check is configured against `/api/health`.
- In this environment, an existing database container accepts local connections but times out for container-to-container TCP probes; the image and Compose configuration are otherwise validated.

## Next session target
- Complete end-to-end Compose runtime validation in an environment with normal container networking.
- Publish the Step 10 handoff commit after CI has run in Jenkins.

## Future phases planned
- backend and database integration with users and bookmarks
- deployment repo for Kubernetes + Terraform

children.text: # Forkify V2 Deployment Repository Separation Strategy
Keep the application codebase and infrastructure codebase decoupled so each repository has a single responsibility and can evolve independently.
This repository will remain responsible for:
A separate repository will be responsible for:
- keeps application development independent from infrastructure provisioning
- reduces accidental coupling between runtime code and deployment configuration
- allows different release cadences for app changes and infrastructure changes
- makes it easier to reuse the app repository across multiple deployment targets
This repository should stay focused on application delivery and local validation only. Infrastructure ownership should not be mixed into application code reviews or feature branches.
1. Feature work happens in the application repository.
2. Docker and CI validation run here.
3. Deployment artifacts are generated or referenced from the deployment repository.
4. Infra changes are reviewed and applied there, separately from app changes.
The application repository may include Docker compose and local environment files, but it should not contain the live cloud deployment state or Kubernetes production configuration.

The repository’s intended path is `npm start`: it starts PostgreSQL, the native backend on `4000`, and Parcel. Because this environment has a Docker container-networking issue, I’ll give you the reliable native-backend workflow first, plus quick health checks and the Docker alternative.

**Recommended local run**

From the repository root:

```bash
cd /workspaces/Forkity-V2
npm start
```

This starts:

- PostgreSQL via Docker
- Backend at http://localhost:4000
- Frontend at http://localhost:1234

Open http://localhost:1234 in your browser.

Validate the backend separately:

```bash
curl http://localhost:4000/api/health
```

Expected response:

```json
{"status":"ok","database":"connected"}
```

If you see a port conflict, stop existing processes first:

```bash
fuser -k 4000/tcp 1234/tcp
npm start
```

Keep the terminal running while using the app. Stop the frontend/backend with `Ctrl+C`; stop PostgreSQL afterward with:

```bash
docker compose stop db
```

The full Docker Compose backend path is also available with:

```bash
docker compose up --build
```

However, the current environment has a container-to-container PostgreSQL networking issue, so `npm start` is the reliable validation path here.

# Stage 11 Deployment Handoff

## Application repository responsibilities

This repository owns:

- frontend, backend, and database source code
- Prisma schema and migration assets
- local Docker Compose
- Dockerfiles for the frontend and backend
- Jenkins validation

Production Kubernetes, Terraform, secrets, and cloud state belong in the separate deployment repository.

## Runtime contract

| Service | Container port | Health or entry point | Required configuration |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| Frontend | 1234 | Browser application | Backend API URL at build or deployment time |
| Backend | 4000 | `GET /api/health` | `DATABASE_URL`, `FORKIFY_API_KEY`, `PORT` |
| PostgreSQL | 5432 | PostgreSQL readiness | Managed by the deployment environment |

The backend image is built with `backend/Dockerfile` using the repository root as its build context because it needs the shared Prisma schema.

## Deployment repository inputs

The deployment repository should provide:

- backend and frontend image references produced from this repository
- a PostgreSQL connection string through a secret
- the Forkify API key through a secret
- an externally reachable backend URL for the frontend build configuration
- readiness and liveness checks based on the backend health endpoint

## Current local validation

```bash
npm start
```

Then open `http://localhost:1234` and check `http://localhost:4000/api/health`.

The local command starts PostgreSQL, generates Prisma Client, starts Express, and starts Parcel. Production deployment remains intentionally separate from this repository.

# Forkify V2 Current Progress

## Date
- 2026-09-24

## Status
- Stages 2 through 8 are complete.
- Stage 9 is complete: end-to-end polish and deployment preparation.
- Stage 10 is complete locally: deployment validation and final handoff preparation.
- Stage 11 is in progress: deployment repository handoff preparation.
- Frontend, backend, PostgreSQL, Docker, Jenkins, and deployment separation are integrated.
- Final local orchestration is available through the root `npm start` command.
- Design polishing remains intentionally deferred until a later stage.

## Completed work
- Reviewed app scope and architecture.
- Confirmed user management and bookmarks are required in the future data model.
- Saved the project plan in the session notes.
- Built the landing-page app shell in frontend/index.html.
- Fixed the view clear/render issue in frontend/js/views/view.js.
- Added upload guard safety in frontend/js/utils/uploadGuard.js.
- Updated add-recipe modal logic in frontend/js/views/addRecipeView.js.
- Added smoke test coverage in frontend/tests/uploadGuard.test.mjs.
- Verified with: npm test and npm run build.

## Verification evidence
- Frontend tests: 4 passing tests, 0 failing tests
- Frontend build: Parcel build succeeded
- Prisma schema validation and database sync succeeded
- Backend health check returned `{"status":"ok","database":"connected"}`
- Root development workflow started backend on port 4000 and frontend on port 1234
- Backend Docker image builds successfully with Prisma and OpenSSL runtime support
- Compose configuration validates successfully
- Jenkins now validates frontend tests/build, backend syntax/Prisma schema, and Compose configuration
- Local startup now generates Prisma Client in the backend dependency tree before launching Express

## Current stage note
- The backend container health check is configured against `/api/health`.
- In this environment, an existing database container accepts local connections but times out for container-to-container TCP probes; the image and Compose configuration are otherwise validated.
- The native local workflow is browser-ready at `http://localhost:1234`.
- Stage 11 handoff details are documented in `stage11-deployment-handoff.md`.

## Next session target
- Configure the frontend backend URL for production deployment builds.
- Complete end-to-end Compose runtime validation in an environment with normal container networking.

## Future phases planned
- backend and database integration with users and bookmarks
- deployment repo for Kubernetes + Terraform

children.text: # Forkify V2 Deployment Repository Separation Strategy
Keep the application codebase and infrastructure codebase decoupled so each repository has a single responsibility and can evolve independently.
This repository will remain responsible for:
A separate repository will be responsible for:
- keeps application development independent from infrastructure provisioning
- reduces accidental coupling between runtime code and deployment configuration
- allows different release cadences for app changes and infrastructure changes
- makes it easier to reuse the app repository across multiple deployment targets
This repository should stay focused on application delivery and local validation only. Infrastructure ownership should not be mixed into application code reviews or feature branches.
1. Feature work happens in the application repository.
2. Docker and CI validation run here.
3. Deployment artifacts are generated or referenced from the deployment repository.
4. Infra changes are reviewed and applied there, separately from app changes.
The application repository may include Docker compose and local environment files, but it should not contain the live cloud deployment state or Kubernetes production configuration.

    <div class="shell">
      <header class="header" id="home">

            <div class="brand__text">forkify</div>

            <ul class="nav__links">
              <li><a class="nav__link nav__link--active" href="#home">Home</a></li>

              <li><a class="nav__link" href="#cookbooks">Cookbooks</a></li>

              <button class="chip-btn" type="button">Log in</button>
              <button class="primary-btn nav__btn--add-recipe" type="button">Get started</button>

          </nav>
        </div>

        <div class="hero">
          <div class="hero__copy">
            <span class="eyebrow">Freshly curated</span>
            <h1>
              Bring <span class="highlight">home-cooked joy</span>
              back to your kitchen.
            </h1>
            <p class="hero__lead">
              Discover vibrant recipes, smart meal ideas, and everyday inspiration
              designed to help you cook with confidence and enjoy every bite.
            </p>

            <div class="hero__actions">
              <button class="primary-btn" type="button">Explore recipes</button>
              <button class="secondary-btn" type="button">Watch the demo</button>
            </div>

            <div class="hero__meta" aria-label="Summary stats">
              <div class="meta-card">
                <span class="meta-card__value">1.2M+</span>
                <span class="meta-card__label">recipes</span>
              </div>
              <div class="meta-card">
                <span class="meta-card__value">4.9/5</span>
                <span class="meta-card__label">average rating</span>
              </div>
              <div class="meta-card">
                <span class="meta-card__value">24k</span>
                <span class="meta-card__label">happy cooks</span>
              </div>
            </div>
          </div>

          <div class="hero__visual" aria-label="Featured recipe preview">
            <div class="visual-card">
              <div class="visual-card__top">
                <span class="badge">Chef’s pick</span>
                <div class="dot-group" aria-hidden="true">
                  <span class="dot"></span>
                  <span class="dot"></span>
                  <span class="dot"></span>

                <span>Easy & vibrant</span>
              </div>

              <div class="mini-card">
                <span class="mini-card__label">This week</span>

                  <span>Sunrise Citrus Bowl</span>
                  <span>★ 4.8</span>
                </div>
              </div>
            </div>
          </div>

        <aside class="sidebar">
          <h2 class="section-heading">Recipes</h2>
          <p class="section-copy">Search the recipe library and open a dish to see its ingredients and directions.</p>
          <form class="search" role="search">
            <input class="search__field" type="text" placeholder="Search for recipes..." aria-label="Search recipes" />
            <button class="primary-btn search__btn" type="submit">Search</button>

          <ul class="results" aria-live="polite"></ul>
          <div class="pagination"></div>

        <section class="recipe-panel">
          <div class="recipe" aria-live="polite"></div>

          <div class="bookmarks-panel__header">
            <span class="eyebrow eyebrow--small">Collections</span>
            <button class="chip-btn nav__btn--bookmarks" type="button">Bookmarks</button>

          <p class="section-copy">Keep the recipes you want to cook again close at hand.</p>
          <ul class="bookmarks__list"></ul>
        </aside>
      </main>

      <section class="cookbooks-panel" id="cookbooks">
        <span class="eyebrow eyebrow--small">Cookbooks</span>
        <h2 class="section-heading">Plan your next table</h2>
        <p class="section-copy">Browse a few starting points for the way you like to cook.</p>

        <div class="cookbooks-grid">
          <article class="cookbook-card">
            <span class="cookbook-card__eyebrow">Weeknight</span>
            <h3>Fast and comforting</h3>
            <p>Simple recipes for full evenings, without compromising on flavor.</p>
          </article>
          <article class="cookbook-card">
            <span class="cookbook-card__eyebrow">Fresh picks</span>
            <h3>Bright and seasonal</h3>
            <p>Colorful ingredients and lighter ideas for meals that feel fresh.</p>
          </article>
          <article class="cookbook-card">
            <span class="cookbook-card__eyebrow">Your kitchen</span>
            <h3>Build your own shelf</h3>
            <p>Bookmark recipes and shape a personal collection worth returning to.</p>
          </article>
        </div>
      </section>
    </div>

    <div class="overlay hidden"></div>

    <div class="add-recipe-window hidden" role="dialog" aria-modal="true">
      <button class="btn--close-modal" type="button" aria-label="Close add recipe window">×</button>

      <form class="upload">
        <h3 class="upload__heading">Add your recipe</h3>

        <div class="upload__column">
          <label for="title">Title</label>
          <input id="title" name="title" type="text" placeholder="e.g. Vegan chili" required />
        </div>

        <div class="upload__column">
          <label for="sourceUrl">URL</label>
          <input id="sourceUrl" name="sourceUrl" type="url" placeholder="https://..." required />
        </div>

        <div class="upload__column">
          <label for="image">Image</label>
          <input id="image" name="image" type="url" placeholder="https://..." required />
        </div>

        <div class="upload__column">
          <label for="publisher">Publisher</label>
          <input id="publisher" name="publisher" type="text" placeholder="Your name" required />
        </div>

        <div class="upload__column">
          <label for="cookingTime">Time</label>
          <input id="cookingTime" name="cookingTime" type="number" min="1" placeholder="45" required />
        </div>

        <div class="upload__column">
          <label for="servings">Servings</label>
          <input id="servings" name="servings" type="number" min="1" placeholder="4" required />
        </div>

        <div class="upload__column">
          <label for="ingredient-1">Ingredients</label>
          <input id="ingredient-1" name="ingredient-1" type="text" placeholder="Quantity, unit, description" />
        </div>

        <div class="upload__column">
          <label for="ingredient-2">Ingredients</label>
          <input id="ingredient-2" name="ingredient-2" type="text" placeholder="Quantity, unit, description" />
        </div>

        <div class="upload__column">
          <label for="ingredient-3">Ingredients</label>
          <input id="ingredient-3" name="ingredient-3" type="text" placeholder="Quantity, unit, description" />
        </div>

        <button class="upload__btn" type="submit">Submit recipe</button>
      </form>
    </div>

    <script type="module" src="./js/controller.js"></script>
  </body>
</html>

# Forkify V2

Forkify V2 is a full-stack redesign of the recipe application originally built during Jonas Schmedtmann's JavaScript course.

## Project boundaries

- `frontend/`: current browser application and Parcel development server
- `backend/`: Express API for users, recipes, and bookmarks
- `database/`: PostgreSQL and Prisma schema/migration assets
- `docs/`: architecture documentation and diagrams

## Local development

Start the full local stack with:

```bash
npm start
```

The frontend is available at `http://localhost:1234` and the backend at `http://localhost:4000`.

## Development sequence

1. Establish the application architecture and preserve the approved visual direction.
2. Migrate the frontend design into React components.
3. Implement the backend API and authentication. (Complete)
4. Add PostgreSQL persistence through Prisma. (Complete)
5. Connect frontend workflows to the backend. (Complete)
6. Add Docker for local and reproducible environments. (Complete)
7. Add Jenkins CI only after the application and design are fully functional. (Complete)

Cloud infrastructure, Terraform, and Kubernetes will be maintained later in a separate deployment repository.
</attachment>

response.value: Two concrete Recipes bugs stand out in the current flow: an empty search leaves the spinner stuck, and opening a recipe before any search can make the results view update against an empty DOM. The detail markup also has an unclosed ingredients list. I’m fixing those behavior issues first, then I’ll tighten the recipe panel’s empty/loading presentation.

The search/detail fixes are in place. I found one more Recipes failure path: after a failed recipe load, the controller still tries to update servings on an empty recipe object. I’m removing that unconditional call and adding a deliberate empty recipe state so the center panel has useful content before a recipe is selected.

        --radius-lg: 24px;
        --radius-md: 18px;
      }

      * {
        box-sizing: border-box;
      }

      html {
        scroll-behavior: smooth;
      }

      body {
        margin: 0;
        font-family: "Manrope", sans-serif;
        background:
          radial-gradient(circle at top left, rgba(255, 122, 89, 0.14), transparent 24%),

          var(--bg);
        color: var(--text);

      a {
        color: inherit;
        text-decoration: none;
      }

      button,

        font: inherit;
      }

        max-width: 1240px;
        margin: 0 auto;
        padding: 24px 24px 56px;
      }

      .header {
        position: relative;
        border: 1px solid rgba(31, 42, 55, 0.06);
        background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.38);
        backdrop-filter: blur(12px);
        -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(12px);
        border-radius: 30px;
        box-shadow: var(--shadow);
        overflow: hidden;
      }

      .header::before {
        content: "";
        position: absolute;
        inset: 0;
        background: linear-gradient(135deg, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.8), rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.22));
        z-index: 0;
      }

      .header__inner {
        position: relative;
        z-index: 1;
        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        justify-content: space-between;
        gap: 24px;

        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        gap: 12px;
        min-width: 180px;
      }

      .brand__mark {
        width: 44px;
        height: 44px;
        border-radius: 14px;
        background: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--primary), #ff9f66);
        display: grid;
        place-items: center;
        box-shadow: 0 14px 26px rgba(255, 122, 89, 0.36);
        color: white;
        font-size: 1.2rem;
        font-weight: 800;
      }

      .brand__text {
        font-weight: 800;
        font-size: 1.35rem;

      .nav {
        display: flex;

        gap: 18px;
        flex-wrap: wrap;
      }

        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        gap: 12px;
        list-style: none;
        padding: 0;
        margin: 0;

      .nav__link {
        padding: 10px 16px;

        font-size: 0.94rem;
        font-weight: 600;
        color: var(--muted);

        background: rgba(31, 42, 55, 0.05);
        color: var(--text);

      .nav__actions {

      }

      .chip-btn,
      .primary-btn,

      .chip-btn {
        background: rgba(31, 42, 55, 0.05);

      .primary-btn {
